title: TLS certificate renewal checklist
when: A site serves HTTPS and the user wants certificates to renew on their own and to be warned well before any of them expires.
prompt:
Goal: Automatic renewal with an ACME client, a reload hook, expiry monitoring and a checklist for the manual parts.
Steps:
1. Inventory each hostname, its certificate paths, the service reading them and who controls DNS.
2. Issue with the HTTP challenge on port 80, or the DNS challenge for wildcards; rehearse on the CA staging endpoint to avoid rate limits.
3. Renew twice daily from a systemd timer or cron; the client acts only under 30 days left.
4. Deploy hook: test the proxy config, then reload (reload keeps connections, restart drops them).
5. Serve the full chain file; private keys mode 600, owned by root or the service user.
6. Daily monitor: echo | openssl s_client -connect host:443 -servername host 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -enddate; alert under 14 days.
7. TLS.md lists hosts, renew and dry run commands, the hook, the monitor and steps when renewal fails.
Quality bar:
- A renewal dry run passes today.
- Alerts fire weeks before expiry.
- Nobody has to remember a date.
Pitfalls:
- Renewal succeeds but nothing reloads, so the old certificate stays live.
- Port 80 closed by the firewall, failing HTTP challenges.
- Names like www or api missing from the certificate.
- HSTS preload before every subdomain serves HTTPS.
Verify:
- [ ] Every host listed with its certificate path.
- [ ] Timer or cron entry shown.
- [ ] Reload hook present.
- [ ] Expiry check documented.
Output: TLS.md checklist plus the timer and hook files.

examples.input: o certificado do meu site expirou de novo, quero automatizar
examples.output: TLS.md with host inventory, twice daily renewal timer, reload hook, openssl expiry check alerting under 14 days
